newsitem.title: CROATIA: Term-loans boost Croatian lending rate to 9.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Term-loans boost Croatian lending rate to 9.7 pct.

text.p: Term-lending at up to 12 percent amid stronger interbank demand boosted Croatia's average money market rate to 9.7 percent on Thursday from 8.2 percent.
Dealers said one-month bank loans at 10 percent accounted for the bulk of today's 58 million kuna settlements, against supply of 95 million.
Call money rose to 11 from 8.0 percent as state investment bank HBOR made a small placement.
The five-10 day rate was up to 8.25 from 7.0 percent.
Wednesday's overnight borrowings by three banks with shortfalls totalled 22.2 million kuna.
The central bank kuna mid-rates for Friday dealings eased to 5.4088 from 5.3613 to the dollar and 3.5622 from 3.5590 against the mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
